# A test that reads a golden file changes behaviour when that file changes,
# and no Go source moves at all. Nothing in a test's own digest would notice,
# so a package's testdata is folded into it.
#
# The state file is the exception. It lives in testdata by default and every
# run rewrites it, so digesting it would make each run invalidate the one
# before it -- reuse would never happen and the file would be pure overhead.

muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1
cmp stdout want-first.txt

# The state file changed, because the run just wrote it. Nothing else did.
muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1
cmp stdout want-reused.txt

# Editing the golden the test compares against retries everything.
cp changed-golden.txt testdata/greeting.html
muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1
cmp stdout want-first.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "greeting"}}Hello, {{.Name}}!{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Name string
}

func Greet(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "greeting", page)
}
-- testdata/greeting.html --
Hello, World!
-- changed-golden.txt --
Hello, Ada!
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"os"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestGreet(t *testing.T) {
	want, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/greeting.html")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	name, _, _ := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(string(want)), ",")
	_ = name

	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Greet(&buf, Page{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := buf.String(); !strings.Contains(strings.TrimSpace(string(want)), "Hello") || got == "" {
		t.Errorf("greeting = %q, want it to render", got)
	}
}
-- want-first.txt --
